rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement can mean that God undertakes to explain the path of guidance.
rows.anchor: علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى بمعنى أن الله تعالى يتكفل ببيان طريق الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can also mean that the path of guidance ultimately leads its traveler to God.
rows.anchor: أن الهدى يوصل صاحبه إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the predicate first restricts guidance to God: guidance from another source is rejected and does not reach Him.
rows.anchor: التقديم في هذه الآية يفيد القصر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative order would retain the basic meaning but would not exclude another source of guidance.
rows.anchor: إن الهدى علينا يتضمن المعنى السابق لكنه لا ينفي كون جهة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic particles answer widespread rejection: people contest God's guidance and claim to define it themselves; emphasis reinforces both exclusivity and the path's destination.
rows.anchor: أكثر الناس يرفضون هذا الأمر لقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the wording been “إن الهدى لعلينا,” it would stress that guidance leads to God but lose the restrictive claim that guidance comes only from Him.
rows.anchor: هذا يؤكد المعنى الثاني ويؤدي إلى فوات معنى الحصر الأول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance statement connects to diverse human endeavors: if people sought God's guidance, their striving would not diverge; the next righteous description exemplifies that guidance.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو ابتغى الناس الهدى عند الله لما تشتت سعيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The givers seek the Hereafter, while misers seek worldly life; both the first and last life belong to God, so people should follow His guidance in each.
rows.anchor: لأن الذي يعطي ويتقي يريد الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ease and hardship may occur in this life or the next, both of which belong to God; people should therefore follow what He commands.
rows.anchor: التيسير والتعسير إما أن يكونا في الدنيا أو في الآخرة ولله الآخرة والأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām emphasizing God's ownership suits the surah's repeated focus on wealth and possession; unlike this context, the wealth-free context of 53:25 omits it.
rows.anchor: فسياق الآيات في سورة الليل جاء كله في الأموال وامتلاكها والتصرف فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an pairs al-ākhirah with al-ūlā, never al-dunyā; al-ūlā is broader, including all earlier affairs of the heavens and earth, whereas al-dunyā denotes human life in this world.
rows.anchor: لم يرد في القرآن الكريم كله ولا مرة واحدة لفظ الدنيا مع الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because al-ūlā is broader than al-dunyā, it aptly expresses the breadth of God's ownership in this surah.
rows.anchor: لما أراد الله تعالى أن يذكر سعة الملك في سورة الليل ناسب أن يأتي بكلمة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He will be pleased” can refer to the pious giver being pleased with his afterlife reward, or to God being pleased with the one seeking His face; both senses apply.
rows.anchor: فيها احتمالين أن تكون للشخص الذي يرضى بثوابه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says Paradise's inhabitants will consult their scholars about what to ask God, and the scholars advise them to ask for His good pleasure, the highest gift.
rows.anchor: قالوا كيف يا رسول الله قال يطلع الله على أهل الجنة فيقول سلوني سلوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's expressive pattern includes generality: it leaves broad references unspecified, including what the night covers, what is avoided, what is given, and what the two outcomes mean.
rows.anchor: السورة كلها في العموم من قوله تعالى (والليل إذا يغشى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah al-Fajr contrasts rich and poor, while al-Balad portrays expenditure and poverty; al-Fajr condemns neglect of orphans and the poor, and al-Balad commands feeding them.
rows.anchor: وفي سورة البلد وصّانا تعالى بالرحمة بهذين الضعيفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Balad's command to feed answers al-Fajr's condemnation of consuming inheritance greedily: as people eat, they should also feed others.
rows.anchor: فكما تأكل يجب أن تطعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Balad presents the full structure of a message: its setting, messenger, recipient, message, and the two groups who respond differently.
rows.anchor: استوفت كل عناصر البلاغ والإرسال

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat lā as an extra particle reinforcing the oath, so “lā uqsim” means “I swear.”
rows.anchor: يقولون (لا) زائدة لتوكيد القسم بمعنى (أقسم)

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: Another reported grammatical view takes lā as negating the oath because the matter is so clear that no oath is needed.
rows.anchor: والغرض منه أن الأمر لا يحتاج للقسم لوضوحه

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: A further view says the negation signals the matter's importance, as in saying that one need not remind someone about a person.
rows.anchor: وقسم قال أنها تنفي لغرض الاهتمام كأن تقول لا أوصيك بفلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here lā reinforces the oath because the subject deserves care and emphasis; the reported interpretations converge on that emphasis.
rows.anchor: تدور (لا) في كل هذه الأمور على أنها توكيد للقسم

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: The most common interpretation is that the Prophet was residing in Mecca, preaching and enduring harm there.
rows.anchor: الرأي الأشهر أنه الحالّ والمقيم أي بمعنى وأنت حال في البلد تبلّغ دعوة ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥill may mean one whose killing is treated as permissible, so the Prophet's sanctity is disregarded in a normally secure city.
rows.anchor: تأتي بمعنى اسم المفعول أي بمعنى (مُستحل)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥill may also mean lawful: at the conquest, God permitted the Prophet to kill or capture those who had violated the city's sanctity, making lā a negation.
rows.anchor: وتأتي (حِل) بمعنى حلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compact word ḥill encompasses residence, violated sanctity, and temporary lawful action; unlike ḥāll, it preserves all meanings and fits the surah's hardship theme.
rows.anchor: ولو جاء باسم الفاعل (حال) لاقتصر على معنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah omits “secure” because its atmosphere concerns hardship and violated sanctity; the Prophet and Companions were unsafe, and the ending details disbelievers' punishment rather than believers' reward.
rows.anchor: جو السورة كلها فيه ذكر للمكابدة والمشقة واستحلال الحرمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “the city” heightens reverence or alarm, as in repeated Qur'anic expressions of awe; it also marks Mecca's changed state at the conquest, as though it became another city.
rows.anchor: تكرار كلمة (البلد) هي في مقام التعظيم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated name also reflects two attributes of Mecca: its ordinary sacred state and its temporary state of fighting at the conquest.
rows.anchor: وكأنه أصبح بلدين فكرّر سبحانه كلمة البلد

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies “a parent and what he begot” as Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: قسم قال المقصود به الإنسان (آدم وذريته)

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the wording generally as every parent and offspring among humans and animals; “what” signals generality, with Adam's family included.
rows.anchor: قسم قال أن المقصود كل والد وما ولد من الأناسي والبهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birth itself entails hardship, linking the oath to humanity's creation in hardship; raising children also requires patience and compassion, matching the surah's ending and the Prophet's struggle.
rows.anchor: الولادة هي المكابدة والشدّة والمشقة

rows.speaker: قسم من المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes direct the charge at those who abuse and torture believers, presuming no one can overcome them.
rows.anchor: قسم من المفسرين يقول هو موجّه للذي يستضعف المؤمنين

rows.speaker: قسم من المفسرين
rows.claim: Others read the address generally: humans created to endure hardship mistakenly think no one can hold them accountable, so they oppress one another.
rows.anchor: وقسم من المفسرين قال أنه الخطاب ليس مقصوراً على هذا الجنس بالذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People rely on wealth and strength as tools for dominance; the Qur'an pairs them when describing abusive power, including wealthy men with sons and a people supplied with wealth and manpower.
rows.anchor: هذان الأمران هما المال والقوة يعتصم بهما الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author ultimately reads the address as directed to humanity generally, which God created to cultivate and improve life.
rows.anchor: هذا الخطاب موجّه للإنسان عموماً الذي خلقه الله تعالى لإصلاح الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elevated paths naturally lead to a steep mountain pass; placing the obstacle after the two elevated ways reflects the terrain and builds a coherent sequence.
rows.anchor: النجد وهو الطريق المرتفع يؤدي إلى العقبة من حيث سلوك الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtihām means entering or crossing forcefully through danger and hardship; it suits the severe obstacle better than the easier verbs “cross” or “pass.”
rows.anchor: الإقتحام فهو الدخول والمجاوزة بشدة ومشقّة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obstacle and its acts of freeing and feeding entail hardship and require strength, connecting both meanings of kabad—difficulty and fortitude—to the following verses.
rows.anchor: اقتحام العقبة فيه مشقة وتعب ويحتاج إلى قوة وفيها ارتباط بمعنيي الكبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fakk raqabah means releasing any restraint, not only manumitting a slave; Qur'anic expiation uses the narrower word taḥrīr, while fakk also covers freeing a debtor or someone wanted for another matter.
rows.anchor: فك رقبة تعني تخليصها من الرق كالغارم والمطلوب لأمر ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image applies across eras to oppressed peoples and to relations in which individuals or rulers subjugate others; social liberation remains a lasting need.
rows.anchor: فك الرقبة هي عقبة من عقبات المجتمع قديماً وحديثاً ومستقبلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broader sense keeps the verse applicable in every age and society, including aid to oppressed populations and relief from forms of personal or governmental coercion.
rows.anchor: فلا يمكن أن تأتي آية في القرآن ولا يكون لها تطبيق لكل زمان ومكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masghabah denotes collective rather than individual hunger, unlike saghab; the passage begins explaining why this word suits the verse.
rows.anchor: المسغبة تعني الجوع العام والجماعي وليس للفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masghabah also conveys hunger with exhaustion, unlike hunger in general; makhmaṣah specifically entails a shrunken abdomen, so the word portrays a severe communal famine when food is scarce.
rows.anchor: المسغبة هي الجوع العام مع التعب والإرهاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿām can mean either the act of eating or the food itself; commentators recognize both senses elsewhere, but this famine context calls for feeding the hungry.
rows.anchor: الطعام تحتمل معنيين أولهما أن تكون بمعنى المصدر لفعل أطعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun iṭʿām is used instead of “that you feed” because the present famine requires immediate feeding, while the latter construction would point to future action.
rows.anchor: هذا المعنى لا يصح في الآية لأن المسغبة قائمة ويجب أن يكون الإطعام فوراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqrabah describes a relative connected by lineage and the womb, combining charity with maintaining kinship and thus making the orphan a priority.
rows.anchor: مقربة: تعني القريب في النسب وفي الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarābah generally denotes kinship by lineage, qurba can include womb kin such as siblings, and maqrabah has a broader scope between those usages.
rows.anchor: القرابة هي عامّة مثل القرابة في النسب، أما القُربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Debtors, people sought for obligations, enslaved people, orphans, and the poor all endure hardship, linking the obstacle's acts to humanity's creation in kabad.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الغارمون والمطلوبون والمسترَقّون واليتامى والمساكين كلهم مكابدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who spent heaps of wealth should have directed some of it to orphans, the poor, and debtors instead of wasting it unjustly.
rows.anchor: كان ينبغي له أن يُنفق على هؤلاء المساكين واليتامى والغارمين شيئاً من ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing and feeding are acts of compassion, and their vulnerable recipients especially need patience, linking the obstacle's tasks to the surah's counsel of mercy.
rows.anchor: فك الرقاب وإطعام المحتاجين من المرحمة وهؤلاء من أحوج الناس إلى الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then can indicate order of mention rather than chronology: faith has a higher rank and is foundational, since no deed benefits a person in the afterlife without faith.
rows.anchor: تراخي رتبة الإيمان عما قبلها لأنه لا ينفع شيء بدون إيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the common pairing “believed and did righteous deeds,” this verse omits the latter because it has already listed freeing and feeding as righteous works.
rows.anchor: يأتي ذكر الذين آمنوا مقرونا بـ (عملوا الصالحات)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the verb in “they counsel one another in patience and they counsel one another in compassion” is stronger than repeating only the preposition or using conjunction alone, because each virtue matters independently.
rows.anchor: تكرار الفعل وهي أقوى التعبيرات لأن فيها توكيد لأهمية كل واحد من الصبر والمرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole surah calls for patience amid the Prophet's harm, child-rearing, choosing the two paths, the obstacle, bondage, famine, care for the vulnerable, and obedience.
rows.anchor: وهذه السورة مبنية كلها على الصبر والمرحمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marḥamah is broader and more encompassing than raḥmah, and the surah's many relationships call for compassion rather than harm.
rows.anchor: المرحمة هي ليست الرحمة فقط ولكنها عامة وهي أهم من الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience comes first because the surah first details hardship and effort, then turns to compassion in feeding orphans and the poor.
rows.anchor: ذكر التواصي بالصبر أولاً ثم التواصي بالمرحمة لأنه تعالى قدّم في السورة ما يحتاج إلى الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Humazah's hoarder thinks wealth makes him immortal; shutting him into Hell's sealed columns fittingly mirrors his hoarding, unlike al-Balad's description of someone who squandered wealth.
rows.anchor: فكما حفظ الكافر المال وجمعه وحسب أنه يخلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Humazah also portrays slander, aggression, and withholding good, making imprisonment apt; al-Balad only names disbelievers, and punishment varies by culpability, as the lowest Fire is mentioned elsewhere.
rows.anchor: والذي يتعدى على الآخرين ينبغي أن يُحبس والحبس يغلق عليه الأبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because al-Balad centers on toil and hardship, it merely identifies believers as the people of the right and does not detail their reward; it does detail disbelievers' fate.
rows.anchor: الكبد كما قلنا سابقاً هو المشقة والمعاناة ولا يناسب جو السورة ذكر الجزاء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes report that revelation paused for days, distressing the Prophet, while opponents claimed his Lord had forsaken him; the surah responds and honors him.
rows.anchor: يذكر أهل التفسير أن الوحي أبطأ على رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause was a test of whether the Prophet valued revelation despite its burden, teaching preachers to persevere through hardship in their mission.
rows.anchor: انه اختبار من الله تعالى للرسول الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duḥā is the time when the sun rises high after sunrise.
rows.anchor: الضحى في اللغة: هو وقت ارتفاع الشمس بعد الشروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sajā has three senses: becoming still, growing deeply dark, and covering something, as in shrouding a dead body.
rows.anchor: سجى في اللغة: لها ثلاث معاني، فهي بمعنى سكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath contrasts the light of revelation, represented by the forenoon, with its interruption, represented by night; the order reflects revelation's prior illumination.
rows.anchor: والضحى هنا يمثل نور الوحي وإشراقه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some interpreters read the interval as restorative repose: night stillness represents relief for the Prophet after exertion.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين أن القسم يشير أن الانقطاع يمثل الاستجمام والسكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sajā brings together stillness and darkness, matching revelation's suspension and loss of light; yaghshā and yasri imply movement and therefore fit less well.
rows.anchor: كلمة سجى جمعت المعاني كلها التي تدل على انقطاع الوحي وسكونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duḥā means the sun's bright rising and the start of people's activity, paired against the still night; daylight spans the whole day and fajr precedes the sun's light.
rows.anchor: الضحى هو وقت إشراق الشمس أما النهار فهو كل الوقت من أول النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of “forsake” is explicit, but the object of “despise” is omitted as a courtesy: speakers avoid even negating hurtful conduct toward someone they honor.
rows.anchor: الذكر من باب التكريم والحذف من باب التكريم أيضاً.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the object with the favorable act of farewell and omitting it with the negative act teaches Muslims respectful speech; the verse honors the Prophet twice.
rows.anchor: جمعت هذه الآية التكريم للرسول من ربه مرتين مرة بذكر المفعول مع فعل التوديع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “your Lord” reassures the Prophet: a Lord nurtures and cares for his servant, and the term conveys the Prophet's particular relationship and protection.
rows.anchor: فالرب هو المربي والموجه والقيم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some interpreters take al-ākhirah as the Hereafter, the life beyond this world.
rows.anchor: إنها ما هو غير الدنيا بمعنى الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Others understand al-ākhirah broadly as whatever comes later in life, not necessarily the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقسم قال انها كل ما يستقبل من الحياة على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ītāʾ is broader than ʿaṭāʾ and includes material or immaterial grants; it may be withdrawn and does not always imply the recipient may dispose of it, whereas a gift belongs to its recipient to use freely.
rows.anchor: الإيتاء يكون لأمور مادية وغيرها (الملك، الحكمة، الذكر)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's care for the orphan, guidance of the Prophet, and relief from poverty confirm that He did not forsake him and that his future is better than his past.
rows.anchor: هذه الآيات مرتبطة بالآيات السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These blessings also echo the oath: orphanhood, error, and need are darkness, while shelter, guidance, and wealth are light.
rows.anchor: واليتم ظلمة والإيواء هو النور وكذلك الضلال ظلمة والهدى نور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preacher should receive questions patiently, whether sincere or provocative, and avoid being baited because provoking the preacher may be the questioner's goal.
rows.anchor: فعليه أن يتسع صدره للسائل مهما كانت نية السائل أو قصده من السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering former hardship encourages gratitude and compassion for people currently afflicted; recalling past harm or embarrassment is acceptable when it helps recognize God's blessings.
rows.anchor: يحسن للإنسان تذكر أيام العسر والضيق لأنه مدعاة للشكر

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the oath's fig and olive as the familiar trees, one fruit seedless and the other containing seeds.
rows.anchor: فقد ذكروا أنه أقسم بنوعين من الشجر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet ate a plate of figs and called it a fruit from Paradise because Paradise's fruit has no seeds; Adam also used fig leaves to cover himself.
rows.anchor: أن التين من شجر الجنة فقد روي أنه أُهدي لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The olive is described as a blessed tree in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وأما الزيتون فإنه شجرة مباركة كما جاء في التنزيل العزيز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author doubts that the fig's alleged Paradisal origin explains the surah's eight verses and eight gates of Paradise, calling that connection likely conjecture despite parallels elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون هذا القول خرصاً محضاً وأنا أميل إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites proposed numerical correspondences: eight Paradise descriptions, seven warnings for Hell, thirty words in al-Qadr, and its word “she” as the twenty-seventh word; he warns many such links may be coincidences.
rows.anchor: وعلى أي حال فإن كثيراً من هذه العلاقات ربما كانت موافقات

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the fig and olive with two Holy Land mountains, called Ṭūr Tīnā and Ṭūr Zaytā in Syriac, where those trees grow.
rows.anchor: إن المقصود بالتين والزيتون جبلان من الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir interprets the oaths as three sites of major messengers with revealed laws: Jerusalem for Jesus, Sinai for Moses, and Mecca for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: هذه محال ثلاثة بعث الله في كل واحد منها نبياً مرسلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the relationship between the two-mountain interpretation and the following oaths is not evident without strained interpretation.
rows.anchor: والعلاقة بين التين والزيتون وما بعدهما ليست ظاهرة على هذا إلا بتكلف

rows.speaker: التبيان في أقسام القرآن
rows.claim: The cited work identifies three sacred sites where major messengers appeared and reads their sequence as rising from Jesus's station to Moses's and finally Muhammad's.
rows.anchor: فأقسم سبحانه بهذه الأمكنة الثلاثة العظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the three-site reading because it makes the relation among the oath's locations clear; he notes a parallel Torah sequence of Sinai, Seir, and Paran for Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الراجح فيما أرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence begins with the fig and the more excellent olive, which God calls blessed; olive serves as fruit, food accompaniment, and lamp oil.
rows.anchor: فقد شهد الله له أنه شجرة مباركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinai ranks above the earlier sites as the mountain where God spoke with Moses, commissioned him, and sent him to Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: ثم أقسم بطور سنين وهو أفضل مما ذكر قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinai is placed beside the olive because the Qur'an describes a tree growing there that yields oil and food; commentators agree this means the olive tree.
rows.anchor: هذه الشجرة هي شجرة الزيتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca, the Prophet's birthplace and mission site and home of the Kaaba, is the most beloved place to God; the oath ascends to the final and noblest revelation.
rows.anchor: فتدرّج من الفاضل إلى الأفضل ومن الشريف إلى الأشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-amīn also invokes trust: Gabriel, the trusted Spirit, conveyed the message-trust to Muhammad, the truthful and trusted, in a city characterized as trustworthy.
rows.anchor: فالرسالة أمانة نزل بها الروح الأمين

rows.speaker: الألوسي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi explains the city's trustworthiness as its protecting whoever enters, as a trustee protects what has been entrusted to him.
rows.anchor: وأمانته أن يحفظ من دخله كما يحفظ الأمين ما يؤتمن عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca is secure before and after becoming a city: Abraham prayed for its safety in both stages, and God answered through the city's sanctuary and pilgrimage rules.
rows.anchor: فهو البلد الآمن قبل الإسلام وبعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-amīn can be an intensive adjective meaning secure, or an adjective in the pattern faʿīl with a passive meaning, “protected”; the city is safe from dangers.
rows.anchor: على هذا (فعيل) للمبالغة بمعنى الآمن

rows.speaker: الألوسي
rows.claim: Al-Alusi reads al-amīn as an active adjective meaning safe or trustworthy, or as passive meaning protected; the city's protection may be figurative or expressed by ellipsis.
rows.anchor: الأمين فعيل بمعنى فاعل أي الآمن

rows.speaker: البحر المحيط
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ says the city is safe for its residents, entrants, birds, and animals, or that al-amīn means a trusted protector or one protected from danger.
rows.anchor: وأمين للمبالغة أي: آمن من فيه ومن دخله وما فيه من طير وحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing al-amīn instead of the Qur'anic al-āmin combines safety and trust, active and passive senses, and literal and figurative meanings.
rows.anchor: أنه باختياره لفظ (الأمين) جمع معنيي الأمن والأمانة

rows.speaker: التبيان في أقسام القرآن
rows.claim: The answer to the oath covers human beginning and end: creation in the best form, return to the lowest state, and the two responses—most are cast down, while believers receive an enduring reward.
rows.anchor: فإنه أقسم بالرسالات على بداية الإنسان ونهايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because revelation offers a human way of life, the answer treats both human nature and its proper method: a sound nature with faith and righteous deeds; a method must accord with human nature to succeed.
rows.anchor: كان الجواب يتعلق بالإنسان طبيعة ومنهجاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is explicitly the subject of creation because this is a statement of His power, beautiful work, and excellent design; Qur'anic praise and beneficence likewise attribute deeds to Him.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه موطن بيان عظيم قدريه وحسن فعله وبديع صنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an names God as creator when displaying blessing and generosity, but uses passive forms when emphasizing human weakness or flaws.
rows.anchor: فانظر كيف أسند الخلق في مقام النهمة والتفضّل إلى ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming God as creator identifies Him as the author of humanity's way of life: its Creator alone knows what suits it, a point a passive construction would not state directly.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يبين أن واضع المنهج للإنسان هو خالق الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is also explicitly the one who returns humanity to the lowest state, showing that He controls both beginning and end; a passive verb might imply a different agent ruined His creation.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يذكر أن بيده البداية والنهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsan taqwīm means humanity was fashioned in the best physical and spiritual form, including appearance, meaning, and understanding.
rows.anchor: صيّره على أحسن ما يكون في الصورة والمعنى والإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks both temporal delay before decline and the great rank-distance between humanity's best form and its lowest state.
rows.anchor: فأفادت (ثم) هاهنا التراخي الزماني والتراخي في الرتبة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take “the lowest of the low” as decrepit old age, with physical and mental decline and loss of understanding.
rows.anchor: فذهب قسم من المفسرين إلى أن المقصود به أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: On the old-age interpretation, the exception means righteous elders retain an uninterrupted reward, credited as in their healthy years; a Prophetic report says a believer returned to decrepitude is credited with former deeds.
rows.anchor: إن المؤمن إذا رد لأرذل العمر كتب له ما كان يعمل في قوته

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Other exegetes understand the lowest state as the lowest place, Hell or its lowest level.
rows.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أن المقصود به أسفل الأماكن السافلة وهو جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Hell interpretation, the exception straightforwardly excludes the righteous from being cast there.
rows.anchor: فالصالحون مستثنون من الرد إلى ذلك
